the region's namespace import (`from plastron.namespaces import bibo, dc, dcmitype, edm, geo, rel, skos, ore, owl, umd, schema, pcdm, dcterms`) is exactly the case the stratum is sampling for -- 18+ genuine term uses (owl.sameAs, edm.Agent, bibo.Letter, dcterms.title, ...), all real, none decorative. But it CANNOT become `from plastron.namespaces import bibo:, dc:, ...`: fetched plastron-utils/src/plastron/namespaces/__init__.py at umd-lib/plastron@4a7f08cc19 (real source, via GitHub) -- it is plain `NAME = Namespace('...')` module attributes, no `__namespaces__` dict anywhere. Unlike the edmondchuc__rdflib-orm region in this same stratum, this module is a real, heavily-used third-party dependency (plastron-utils, its own package) we cannot patch the way a same-repo test shim can add one line -- so the import stays ordinary Python for every one of these dozen namespaces, uncredited. This is the strongest instance yet of the finding the batch reminder anticipated: a project namespace module lacking `__namespaces__` blocks the construction regardless of how heavily its terms are actually used.
